lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Visually group the two Ridgeway degrees and reduce repeated institution and location text.
items.because: Both degrees are from the same institution.

items.says: Reorder the résumé as Education, Quantitative/Research Experience, Projects, Additional Experience, and Skills.
items.because: The bakery role currently appears before the more relevant Northpeak and research work.

items.says: Limit the bakery entry to its strongest one or two bullets.
items.because: It is less relevant to quant applications.

items.says: Keep the résumé to one page if possible.
items.because: A second page is justified only by a substantial publication record.

items.says: Use a consistent date style, preferably en dashes rather than hyphens.
Use consistent US spelling, punctuation, capitalization, and formatting.
items.because: The résumé is set in the USA.

items.says: Clearly distinguish live results, paper trading, out-of-sample backtests, and model-selection results.
items.because: Several performance claims could otherwise be mistaken for realized live performance.

items.says: Audit every performance number for period, benchmark, costs, selection, untouched data, uncertainty, and whether it was simulated.
Ensure team and desk outcomes are not presented as solely yours.
items.because: Attribution must be accurate.

items.says: Review all Northpeak bullets for confidentiality before external distribution.
items.because: The entry discusses signals, reuse, portfolio-manager approval, and allocations.

items.says: Make the name visually prominent but not oversized.
Label the code link by platform or purpose instead of using a bare URL.
items.because: Recruiters should immediately know whether it is GitHub, a portfolio, or something else.

items.says: Ensure the linked profile contains polished repositories relevant to the résumé's claims.
Add LinkedIn only if it is complete and consistent with the résumé.
Confirm that “Ph.D. candidate” is the institution's official degree status.
items.because: If candidacy has not formally been conferred, a different status is needed.

items.says: Consider adding a dissertation area, advisor, or short research focus.
items.because: It could directly support quant applications.

items.says: Add honors or GPA only if they are strong and useful.
Quantify or clarify performance against the weekly labour budget.
items.because: The current phrasing establishes compliance but not scale or degree of performance.

items.says: Change “labour” to US spelling.
items.because: The British spelling conflicts with the résumé's US setting.

items.says: Remove the awkward mid-phrase line break in the final PDF.
State whether the reduction from 12% to 7% was sustained and over what period.
Use the precise business waste metric rather than “unsold bread” if that measure excludes some inventory outcomes.
items.because: Discounted, donated, or discarded inventory may not be included.

items.says: Add the desk or asset class if it is not confidential.
items.because: It would provide useful context.

items.says: Define the metric meant by “risk-adjusted returns.”
items.because: The phrase is too broad to evaluate and may overlap with the later Sharpe claim.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% improvement is relative or absolute.
State whether the 35% result came from a backtest, paper trading, or live performance.
items.because: The current wording can sound like realized live performance.

items.says: Clarify whether this and the later Sharpe claim describe the same result.
items.because: The two performance bullets may overlap.

items.says: State whether the six years included a final untouched test period isolated from repeated tuning.
items.because: Purging and embargoing do not by themselves prevent model-selection overfitting.

items.says: Tighten the long explanatory clause about point-in-time validation.
items.because: It defines the concept at textbook length.

items.says: Avoid implying perfect absence of leakage unless all timing and execution details were verified.
items.because: Feature timestamps, labels, joins, roll construction, and execution assumptions can still introduce leakage.

items.says: Verify that “feature store” is the technically accurate classification.
items.because: The work may instead have been a research pipeline or library.

items.says: Add meaningful scale or performance information if available.
items.because: Instruments, data volume, or time saved could make the engineering impact clearer.

items.says: Clarify your ownership if the feature store was collaborative.
Ensure disclosure of the two later signal projects is permitted.
Clarify whether the allocation was actually deployed or merely approved.
items.because: Approval should not imply implementation.

items.says: Separate internship-time approval from any later live results.
items.because: The allocation was scheduled for the next quarter.

items.says: Ensure the portfolio-manager approval and allocation timing are not confidential.
Treating the best Sharpe from 400 tested configurations as expected live Sharpe is statistically invalid.
items.because: It ignores multiple-testing selection bias and uncertainty.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1.1-to-1.5 change applies to the signal, a combined desk book, or a simulated portfolio.
items.because: The object whose Sharpe improved is ambiguous.

items.says: Make the backtested status more prominent.
items.because: The result should not be mistaken for live performance.

items.says: Confirm that the out-of-sample period remained untouched after all feature and parameter choices.
Clarify whether costs include realistic fees, spread, slippage, latency, turnover, and market impact.
Keep only one primary Northpeak performance bullet if this and the 35% claim describe the same result.
items.because: The claims overlap.

items.says: The order-book imbalance result appears duplicated in the Kaggle entry.
items.because: The nearly identical result raises questions about ownership, confidentiality, and double-counting.

items.says: Verify that the performance information is not proprietary.
Identify any formal program associated with the assistantship accurately.
items.because: The dates alone do not provide that context.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker can invalidate the claimed 2,000-run Monte Carlo study.
items.because: It can create duplicate random streams rather than independent simulations.

items.says: Replace “my proof” with the impersonal style used elsewhere.
Verify that the logarithmic improvement uses assumptions comparable to the previous bound.
items.because: Statistical recruiters may probe whether the bounds are directly comparable.

items.says: Identify your contribution accurately if the proof or paper is coauthored.
Use “under review at JASA” only if the manuscript was submitted and remains under review.
Add the paper title or a publications section if the work is public.
Clarify whether you independently wrote all 12 problem sets or contributed to them.
Give the basis and response count for the 4.8/5 rating if space permits.
items.because: The rating is more meaningful with a substantial response count.

items.says: Shorten or remove the teaching bullet if space is needed.
items.because: It is less important than research for quant roles.

items.says: Link the public R package through the portfolio or a project or publications entry.
Clarify whether the 3,000 downloads were from CRAN, GitHub, or another source.
State your ownership accurately if the package had co-maintainers.
Mention testing, documentation, or performance if notable and space allows.
Clarify whether the ongoing project is active research, completed analysis under revision, or a working paper in development.
items.because: It has been listed as ongoing since January 2024.

items.says: Add a repository or paper link if the project is public.
State whether the 7% reduction is an average, median, or aggregate across indices.
Confirm that model and hyperparameter selection were separated from final out-of-sample evaluation.
State the forecast horizon if it is central.
items.because: Without it, the result is harder to assess.

items.says: Verify that the HAR-RV baseline was fairly tuned with the same information set.
Verify that the Diebold–Mariano tests account for overlapping forecasts and serial correlation.
Define the two crisis periods by date or event.
items.because: The current reference has no antecedent.

items.says: Keep statistical significance distinct from economic significance.
Ensure the Holm correction used the correct family of hypotheses.
Make it unambiguous whether you presented the paper.
Link the paper if it is available.
Replace the 12-page length with a stronger indicator if available.
items.because: Acceptance, audience, or public availability may be more informative.

items.says: Add the actual competition name if it is public.
Include the final rank, percentile, medal, or score if respectable.
items.because: Without an outcome, the entry feels incomplete.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution within the team of three.
Make the bullet more specific or remove it.
items.because: It is too generic and gives no distinguishing feature type, model family, responsibility, or measurable contribution.

items.says: Define what metric the 0.02 gap measures.
items.because: A raw number is meaningless without the competition metric.

items.says: Do not treat closure of the validation-to-leaderboard gap as proof that leakage was removed.
items.because: Time-grouped folds may reduce temporal leakage, but the gap is not direct proof that all leakage was eliminated.

items.says: Confirm that leaderboard feedback was not repeatedly used as another tuning set.
The futures-book Sharpe result appears to duplicate the Northpeak order-book imbalance result.
items.because: The dataset, period, methodology, and outcome are nearly identical.

items.says: Give the Sharpe claim clear provenance within the Kaggle competition.
items.because: Kaggle competitions normally use defined leaderboard metrics rather than a separate futures-book Sharpe.

items.says: Remove the claim from Kaggle if it was internship work.
items.because: It belongs under Northpeak and may be confidential.

items.says: If this was distinct work, differentiate its dataset, period, methodology, and outcome.
items.because: The résumé should not double-count the same accomplishment.

items.says: PyTorch and Kafka are incorrectly grouped as programming languages.
items.because: They are a framework and infrastructure rather than programming languages.

items.says: Add SQL if you can use it competently.
items.because: It is commonly expected in quant and data roles.

items.says: List relevant tools such as Git, Linux, cloud platforms, databases, or distributed systems if defensible.
items.because: The section does not fully reflect the production-like data work described elsewhere.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled and should be “econometrics.”
Standardize capitalization in the methods list.
Add the most role-relevant demonstrated methods that are currently omitted.
items.because: The résumé shows Monte Carlo methods, market microstructure, forecasting, backtesting, and statistical learning.

items.says: Organize “gradient boosting” into a more consistent category.
items.because: It is narrower and more tool-like than the other listed methods.
